reason: E1 and E2 directly support the mechanism that a continuous B2 matrix limits ductility and that phase inversion via annealing improves compressive ductility while maintaining strength in a specific RHEA. However, the cited evidence is entirely from a different alloy system (Al0.5NbTa0.8Ti1.5V0.2Zr) and reports only compressive ductility, not tensile ductility or impact energy release, so the transfer to HfZrTiTa0.53 and the predicted tensile outcomes are unsupported extrapolations.
premises: Continuous ordered B2 matrix causes poor ductility in RHEAs
Phase inversion to continuous BCC matrix with discrete B2 precipitates improves ductility
Controlled annealing can induce this phase inversion
The inverted microstructure retains high yield strength
These findings from Al0.5NbTa0.8Ti1.5V0.2Zr are transferable to HfZrTiTa0.53
